digest.component_or_area: op-cert service signing and key provisioning
propositions: Op-cert presently performs per-job boto3/SSM key lookup and patches process-global state, creating concurrency hazards and coupling the application to a single secret store
Startup binding must validate exactly one source (REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY), copy the key to a process-owned 0700 dir / 0600 file, and never re-read the deployment source

Both signing producer chains (completion via transition_close.sign_completion_verdict and plan-review via attest.py/generation.sign_manifest) must accept and forward an optional context-local OpcertSigner binding instead of reading os.environ
The op-cert container runtime must have no SSM/boto3/region dependency; the key is materialized outside the app by fetch-secrets.sh and bind-mounted read-only with REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH
Concurrent and timed-out jobs must prove context-local isolation of signer, principal, and push policy with one immutable startup signer and no workspace push remote
Developer-local signing paths (close/review-plan callers without a binding) retain prior env/genesis resolution for backward compatibility
